ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is a chord of the circle $\odot O$, and point $C$ is a point on the circle $\odot O$. Given that $\angle ACB = 55^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle ACB = 55^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle AOB = 2\angle ACB = 110^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle AOB = \boxed{110^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A and B are two points on the circle, O is the center, and the angle ∠AOB is the central angle subtending chord AB. Point C is also on the circle, and ∠ACB is an inscribed angle whose sides pass through A and B, so it subtends the same chord/arc AB as ∠AOB. From the text, use the given ∠ACB = 55°. Apply the circle theorem that a central angle is twice any inscribed angle subtending the same arc. Therefore compute ∠AOB = 2 × 55° = 110°.
